notes: Fix for the lead/lug errors: the motor-controller board's motor terminal ports A1, A2, B1 and B2 are now kind 'lead', because the motor's wires are leads clamped in the screw terminals. The battery terminals VIN+ and VIN- stay as lugs.

Fix for the unconnected ball caster: I added the cardboard box chassis (box1, new type chassis-box). The tutorial uses a small cardboard or plastic box, and it is where the caster is screwed. Step 1 left the box out. The box also holds the motors (adhesive putty or tape), the Pi and the battery holder.
The box has no ports, so edges to it use null ports. The Pi and the battery holder only rest in the box (contact).

The motor controller board is not in the catalogue, so it is a new type. It plugs onto the first 26 GPIO pins of the Pi. The catalogue's raspberry-pi-5 only has a GPIO_HEADER port, so the join is GPIO_HEADER to GPIO_HEADER. The motor signals on GPIO 7, 8, 9 and 10 run through that header.
Motor 1 is on terminal block A and motor 2 on B. Motor wires are symmetric, so each motor's polarity is chosen in software (the pin order in the Robot() call).
Battery holder red wire (positive) goes to the + terminal and black wire (negative) to the - terminal. The four AA cells are in series in the holder.
The wheels are pushed onto the motor axles. The dc-motor catalogue entry has no axle port, so these joins have no motor port.
The USB power bank powers the Pi through a USB cable to the Pi's USB-C power port. The usb-cable type has no ports.
The optional breadboard, distance sensor and line sensors are not built, as in step 1.
